Topic 6 of 18

DHIS2 Data Sets

Step by Step Guide: Building the Data Set and Testing Data Entry

Purpose of this guide

With the data elements and category combinations in place, this guide builds the data set that becomes the reporting form, and then tests it through data entry. Before you start, log in and open the Maintenance app as shown in Topic 1. After completing each step, insert a screenshot of your DHIS2 screen in the screenshot area.

Step 1: Create the Data Set

Create the dataset that will contain all the data elements for the reporting form.

Click: Data Sets → + New
Example:

Name: Monthly Malaria Service Reporting
Short Name: Malaria Monthly
Period Type: Monthly
Description: Monthly reporting of malaria services and outcomes
Expected result: The dataset is created and available for configuration.
  1. 1Name (*). The full name of the data set. It appears in the data entry app.
  2. 2Short name (*). A shorter name used in reports.
  3. 3Description. What the data set is for.
  4. 4Expiry days and open future periods. Leave both at 0 while you are testing.
  5. 5Period type (*). Monthly, because facilities report once a month.
  6. 6Category combination (*). None for the data set itself. The breakdown sits on the data elements.
Step 2: Add Data Elements to the Data Set

Add all the data elements that belong to the reporting dataset.

Open the Data Set → Configure/Edit data elements → Add the required data elements

Recommended order

  1. Malaria Testing
  2. Malaria Results
  3. Treatment
  4. Outcomes
Expected result: All required data elements are associated with the dataset.
  1. 1Search. Type part of a name to shorten the list.
  2. 2Available data elements. Everything in the system that is not in this data set yet.
  3. 3Arrow buttons. Move the selected data element across, or back.
  4. 4Selected data elements. The ten malaria data elements that belong to this form.
  5. 5ASSIGN ALL. Moves everything on the left across. Do not use it here.
  6. 6REMOVE ALL. Clears the right hand list, if you need to start again.
  7. 7SAVE. Saves the data set with its data elements.
Step 3: Assign the Data Set to Organisation Units

Assign the dataset to the organisation units that are expected to submit reports.

Open Data Set → Organisation Units → Select the reporting organisation units
Example:

Sierra Leone → Bo District → Selected Health Facilities
Expected result: The dataset becomes available for data entry at the assigned organisation units.
  1. 1Count. How many organisation units are ticked.
  2. 2The tree. Click the small arrow to open a district, then tick the facilities that report.
  3. 3Level and group. Tick every unit at one level, or in one group, in one click.
  4. 4SELECT ALL. Ticks the whole country. Use it only when every facility reports.
  5. 5SAVE. Saves the assignment.
Step 4: Create Sections

Organise the dataset into logical sections so that the final data-entry form is easy to use.

Data set list → row menu → Manage sections → blue plus button
Suggested sections:

1. Reporting Information
2. Malaria Testing
3. Malaria Results
4. Treatment
5. Outcomes
Expected result: The dataset is divided into clear reporting sections.
  1. 1DATA SET tab. The orange line shows the tab you are on.
  2. 2Search. Type part of the name to find your data set quickly.
  3. 3Your data set. Monthly Malaria Service Reporting.
  4. 4Form type. Default until sections exist. It changes to Section once you add them.
  5. 5Row menu. The three dots at the end of the row.
  6. 6Manage sections. Opens the section list for this data set. The same menu holds Edit compulsory data elements and Sharing settings, which we use in Steps 6 and 8.
  1. 1Data set section management. The back arrow returns to the data set list.
  2. 2The data set. The sections you make here belong to this data set only.
  3. 3Name column. Your sections appear here, in the order they will show on the form.
  4. 4Blue plus button. Opens the Add section window.
  1. 1Name (*). The heading users will see on the form, such as Malaria Testing.
  2. 2Code. Optional. A short code such as mal_test.
  3. 3Description. Optional. A note about what belongs in the section.
  4. 4Totals and grouping. Leave all three boxes unticked for a simple form.
  5. 5Category combo filter. Leave it as No filter, so every data element is offered.
  6. 6Search. Type part of a name to shorten the list below.
  7. 7Data elements. The two lists where you choose the fields of this section.
  8. 8SAVE. Saves the section. CANCEL closes the window without saving.
Step 5: Add Data Elements to Each Section

Select the appropriate data elements for each section and arrange them in the order in which users should report the information.

Example — Malaria Testing:

Suspected malaria cases
RDT tested
Microscopy tested
Expected result: Each section contains only the fields relevant to that part of the report.
  1. 1Available data elements. The data elements of this data set that are not in this section.
  2. 2Arrow buttons. Move one data element at a time, so the order stays under your control.
  3. 3Selected data elements. The fields of this section, in the order they appear on the form.
  4. 4ASSIGN ALL. Moves everything on the left across. Do not use it here.
  5. 5REMOVE ALL. Clears the right hand list, if you need to start again.
  6. 6Up and down arrows. Change the order of the selected fields.
  7. 7SAVE. Saves the section with its data elements.
  1. 1The section. Malaria Testing now appears in the list.
  2. 2Row menu. Edit the section, or delete it, from here.
  3. 3Section saved. A short message confirms the save.
  4. 4Blue plus button. Add the next section, and repeat until all sections exist.
Step 6: Make Required Fields Compulsory

Identify the fields that must be completed before a report can be considered complete.

Data Set → Edit Compulsory Data Elements

Important

Do not make every field compulsory. Only mark fields as compulsory when the programme reporting requirements require them.

Expected result: Users are required to complete the selected fields during data entry.
  1. 1The data set. The compulsory list belongs to this data set only.
  2. 2Available data elements. Everything in the data set that is not compulsory.
  3. 3Arrow buttons. Move a data element across to make it compulsory.
  4. 4Compulsory data elements. Only the fields the programme insists on. Keep this list short.
  5. 5SAVE. Saves the compulsory list.
Step 7: Create Validation Rules

Create rules that identify logically impossible or inconsistent combinations of reported values.

Examples:

RDT Positive ≤ RDT Tested
Microscopy Positive ≤ Microscopy Tested
Malaria Deaths ≥ 0
Open: Validation Rules → + New
Expected result: DHIS2 can identify reporting inconsistencies when the form is validated.
  1. 1Name (*). Say what the rule checks, so the message makes sense when it appears.
  2. 2Importance. Medium is fine for a reporting check.
  3. 3Period type (*). Monthly, the same as the data set.
  4. 4Operator (*). less_than_or_equal_to, so the left side may not be greater than the right.
  5. 5Left side. The value being checked, here RDT Positive.
  6. 6EDIT. Opens the expression builder, where you pick the data element.
  7. 7Right side. The value it is compared with, here RDT Tested.
  8. 8SAVE. Saves the rule.
Step 8: Configure Data Set Sharing

Configure metadata sharing so that the appropriate users and user groups can access the dataset.

Data Set → Sharing / Access

Check

  • Who can view the dataset?
  • Who can enter data?
  • Who can complete the dataset?
  • Which organisation units are available to the users?
Expected result: The intended users can access the dataset according to their permissions.
  1. 1Sharing settings. Opened from the row menu of the data set.
  2. 2Add users and user groups. Type a name to give a group access.
  3. 3Who has access. Public access first, then each user group you added.
  4. 4Metadata. Whether they can see or change the form itself.
  5. 5Data. Whether they can enter data with the form.
  6. 6APPLY. Saves the sharing settings.
Step 9: Final Review of the Configuration

Review the complete form before deploying it to users.

  • Check every data element.
  • Check every section.
  • Check compulsory fields.
  • Check validation rules.
  • Check organisation-unit assignment.
  • Check user access.
  • Test the reporting period.
  • Test with realistic and invalid data.
  • Test on the devices that users will actually use.
Expected result: The complete DHIS2 data-entry form is ready for user acceptance testing.

Final Checklist

  • ☐ Data set created
  • ☐ Data elements added to the data set
  • ☐ Organisation units assigned
  • ☐ Sections created
  • ☐ Data elements assigned to sections
  • ☐ Compulsory fields configured
  • ☐ Validation rules created
  • ☐ Sharing and access configured
  • ☐ Configuration reviewed before data entry starts
